title: Verifier-Grounded Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study
abstract: We report a preregistered, verifier-grounded comparison of a deterministic template baseline and a single-pass LLM generator (gpt-5-mini) on 120 programmatically synthesized intent→configuration tasks spanning three topology classes. Using a deterministic open validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a paired-binary analysis, both conditions achieved verifier pass rate 120/120. Paired difference = 0.00 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00], 10,000 resamples); McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. We archive the full artifact bundle and trace evidence. We interpret this degenerate (perfect‑agreement) outcome in light of (1) shared-initial generation semantics used in execution, (2) coupling between the task-synthesis transformation rules and the validator constraints, and (3) the synthetic, template-driven task bank. We discuss threats to validity and prescribe extensions required to assess operational generality.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to convert operator intent into device configurations to accelerate NetOps activities. Prior work documents both promise and failure modes (e.g., incorrect ordering of change steps, ACL/BGP-policy regressions, and hallucinated commands) and motivates verifier-grounded evaluation because token-level metrics miss operationally relevant semantic errors [1,3]. We preregistered CAND-2026-001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1 to study whether a single-pass LLM generator (declared_model_version: gpt-5-mini) achieves higher verifier pass rates than a deterministic template baseline on N=120 intent→configuration tasks. Our contributions: (i) a preregistered, fully archived benchmark and execution artifacts; (ii) a confirmatory paired analysis with an open deterministic validator; and (iii) an artifact-grounded discussion of what a degenerate (perfect-agreement) result implies for operational evaluation.
sections.related_work: Prior surveys and applied studies evaluate intent→configuration systems, LLM-based configuration synthesis, and verifier-based validation in NetOps. Representative references motivate verifier-grounded assessment and show that tools such as Batfish and related control-plane verifiers are essential to capture reachability and policy preservation beyond textual correctness [1,2]. Our work differs by (a) using a preregistered paired confirmatory design, (b) archiving every model call and validator trace, and (c) explicitly documenting generation semantics and contamination checks so readers can reproduce and audit the null/degenerate outcome.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and execution: The experimental plan (CAND-2026-001-NetConfig-Semantic-v1) was frozen prior to execution and is recorded in the evidence bundle (preregistration SHA-256: 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37). Task generation: 120 intent→configuration tasks were programmatically synthesized and unit-tested; tasks cover three topology classes (edge, datacenter, multi‑AS), 40 tasks per class (manifested in execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Conditions: (A) deterministic template baseline, produced by the deterministic task-transformation pipeline; (B) gpt-5-mini single‑pass generation accessed via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter (execution/model_configuration.json, sha256 a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Generation semantics: the confirmatory runs used the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (the same initial candidate was provided to both conditions in each pair). Representative shared_initial artifacts and raw responses are archived (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt; see artifact hash manifest). Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0) produced a binary verifier pass/fail and detailed validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json). Primary estimand and analysis: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline across N=120 pairs; inference via 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 replicates, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two-sided test per the preregistered analysis plan. Contamination detection: preregistered heuristics (exact-match OR normalized 5-gram overlap >= 0.95 flagged as 'suspected_contamination'; normalized Levenshtein >= 0.90 flagged as 'high_overlap'; self-BLEU aggregation also computed). All thresholds and detection algorithms are those recorded in the preregistration; contamination outputs and the empty results are archived (analysis/contamination_summary.csv, sha256 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Reproducibility: every prompt, model response, validator trace, seed, and file hash is archived under execution/ and analysis/ paths; the full hash manifest is execution/execution_manifest.json.
sections.results: Execution: completed pairs = 120/120; no infrastructure failures; model-call count = 120 (shared-initial generation per pair). Verifier outcomes: baseline successes = 120/120 (pass rate 1.00); gpt-5-mini successes = 120/120 (pass rate 1.00). Contingency table: n_11 = 120, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, sha256 9f25790c7eeaafb3562e0710e0cf10b7a47a55ea00fcbcf02eee324f79afafe7). Estimated paired difference = 0.00. Bootstrap 95% CI (10,000 replicates, seed=1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Representative validator-scored episodes and traces are archived (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json, sha256 0d56c1add7c5a57fff893fe02bd395c435a422f5431376e439875577a8431063) and show validated final_state objects with required fields and validation_status = true. Contamination-detection results: no confirmatory items were flagged; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (sha256 389227f0...). All analysis artifacts, logs, and the deterministic reconciliation report (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) are provided for audit.
sections.discussion: Interpretation of the degenerate outcome. The observed perfect agreement (120/120 passes in both conditions) is a valid experimental fact under the preregistered pipeline and archived artifacts. However, this degenerate result must be interpreted conservatively for operational generality because of three artifact-backed facts: (1) shared-initial generation semantics: confirmatory generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" supplied an identical initial candidate to both conditions per pair (see execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/responses/* shared-initial files), so the paired comparisons used identical canonical candidates for baseline and LLM in the confirmatory seed_0 runs; (2) coupling of task synthesis and validator constraints: the validator enforces the same intent-constraint rules that were used by the deterministic transformation pipeline to construct the reference/gold answers (the task generator and validator specification artifacts are co-archived under execution/ and transformation_manifest.json), which creates evaluation conditions that favour the deterministic templates and any generator closely matching the template grammar; and (3) synthetic, templated task bank: tasks were programmatically synthesized from structured templates and therefore exhibit regular solution forms that are easier for both deterministic transforms and constrained LLM decoding to match. Statistical note on degeneracy: with zero discordant pairs the McNemar test is vacuous (p=1.0) and the bootstrap distribution of the paired difference is degenerate ([0.00,0.00]); this documents absence of observed discordance in this sample but does not establish equivalence beyond the sampled, constrained task+validator setting. Operational implications and next steps: verifier-grounded metrics are necessary for operationally meaningful evaluation; future work should (i) remove or reduce shared-initial coupling to exercise independent model generation, (ii) expand to less templated, heterogeneous tasks and adversarial cases, (iii) sample multiple independent seeds per task to quantify seed sensitivity, and (iv) include complementary validators/emulators that exercise dynamic control-plane interactions (BGP policy effects, ACL reachability under failures) and vendor idiosyncrasies. We have archived all artifacts to enable such follow-up studies.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic confirmatory protocol, both a deterministic template baseline and gpt-5-mini single‑pass generation produced verifier-valid configurations on the N=120 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (paired difference 0.00, 95% CI [0.00,0.00], McNemar p=1.0). The evidence is archived and reproducible. The null/degenerate result reflects the controlled task bank, shared-initial generation semantics, and validator/task coupling; it should not be taken as evidence of LLM operational equivalence in heterogeneous production settings. We release the full artifact bundle (execution/* and analysis/*) and recommend that verifier-grounded evaluations proceed with broader, less templated tasks, multi-seed sampling, and multiple validator modalities to assess real-world reliability.

No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Task-generation and baseline derivation: deterministic-template baseline outputs were produced by the deterministic task-transformation pipeline described in the preregistration and archived under execution/transformation_manifest.json (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl entries). Confirmatory generation semantics: the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" was used for the confirmatory seed_0 runs, i.e., an identical canonical candidate was supplied to both conditions in each pair; representative shared-initial responses and their SHA-256 hashes are archived under execution/responses/ (examples: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt sha256 8f38c8be..., execution/responses/task-000002-shared-initial.txt sha256 ae967f70..., full manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). For the confirmatory seed_0 dataset no items were flagged; the computed results and empty summary are archived at analysis/contamination_summary.csv (sha256 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Contact and provenance: see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl for full provenance, file lists, and deterministic checks (all file hashes published).
limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: tasks were programmatically synthesized from deterministic templates and transformation rules; this favors regular solution forms and limits generality to heterogeneous operational intents.

Shared-initial generation semantics in confirmatory runs: the preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" supplied identical canonical candidates to both conditions per pair for seed_0; this reduces independent variability between conditions and must be considered when interpreting the paired comparison (see execution/responses/* shared-initial files and execution/transformation_manifest.json).

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: the primary design used one canonical seed per task (seed_0) for the paired analysis; exploratory multi-seed analyses were reserved but are not part of the confirmatory result presented here.

Validator-task coupling: the deterministic validator enforces the same semantic constraints used to synthesize reference answers; this coupling increases the probability that both deterministic templates and generators closely matching the template grammar will pass, limiting construct validity for open operational distributions.

Possible training-data exposure: exact-proof that the model was not exposed to template artifacts during pretraining cannot be provided; preregistered contamination heuristics (exact-match, normalized 5-gram overlap >= 0.95, normalized Levenshtein >= 0.90, and self-BLEU) were computed and found no confirmatory flags (analysis/contamination_summary.csv), but residual uncertainty remains.

Single-model, single-validator result: findings apply to gpt-5-mini under the recorded execution conditions and validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); they do not generalize to other LLM families, multi-step agentic pipelines, or different validators/emulators.
